newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says its troops won't enter Bangui conflict.
newsitem.headline: France says its troops won't enter Bangui conflict.

text.p: France insisted on Thursday that its troops would not get involved in an internal conflict between rebels and the government in the Central African Republic, only hours after they were involved in their first serious fighting.

"The situation in Bangui is difficult because at this moment a number of mutineers and rebels are threatening the balance of the country, but there is no question of French troops entering an internal conflict," Defence Minister Charles Million said.

He told reporters after meeting his Italian counterpart that the role of the French troops permanently stationed in the strategic country was limited to "participating in maintaining legality and protecting our nationals".

Asked whether that meant that Paris was ordering its soldiers to defend President Ange Felix Patasse's embattled administration against the third mutiny in a year, which erupted on November 16, he repeated: "French troops will not interfere in any way in an internal Central African Republic conflict."
Witnesses in Bangui said army mutineers clashed with loyalist forces and French troops on Thursday in worsening fighting.

An official defence ministry source in Paris said the French soldiers had fired back in "legitimate self-defence" when the rebels fired four rocket-propelled grenades at the luxury French-owned Sofitel hotel during the night.

"Clashes took place between 2.30 and 6.00 a.m. between the mutineers and loyalist forces. The Sofitel was targeted. Four RPGs were fired at the hotel. It seems two hit the hotel without causing casualties," the source said.
French forces came under attack while they were evacuating the hotel and returned fire in self-defence, after which calm was restored, he said.
The Defence Ministry also said French troops had reopened a road from the French embassy to the hotel which had been blocked by the mutineers.
